title: Tell a 👍/👎 to the bot's next turn once, even in the same second as its reply
body:
## What broke
CI rust on #299 (run 41925843282) failed in `tests/reactions_replies_test.rs::other_reactions_are_feedback_the_bots_next_turn_hears_about`, which #299 doesn't touch. The `fb2` turn was told the 👍/👎 again after the `fb1` turn had already been told them.

## Root cause (confirmed)
`reactions_since_last_reply` (`src/db/reactions.rs`) picked reactions with `julianday(r.created_at) >= last.at`, where `last.at` is the bot's newest message in the chat. Both `created_at` values come from `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, which has 1-second precision. When a reaction landed in the same second as the bot's reply, it still counted as new after that reply, so the next turn heard the same 👎 again. With the fake CLI's fast replies this happens when the test runs inside one second. In real use a bot could be told the same 👎 twice.

## Fix
- `message_reactions.told INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, added by an idempotent `ALTER` guarded by `pragma_table_info`, the same as `reply_to_message_id`. A new database and one from #296 end up with the same schema. The `CREATE TABLE` is unchanged.
- `feedback_note` marks the reactions it puts into a turn's prompt as told (`Database::mark_told`, matched on message and reaction).
- `reactions_since_last_reply` also requires `told = 0`. The "since the last reply" time rule stays, so reactions in existing databases that were made before the bot's last reply are still never told, and no backfill is needed.
- A changed reaction resets `told` (as it already reset `answered`). Clearing and re-setting a reaction makes a new row, which is news again.
- The note's wording and the history marks ("(The person reacted 👎 to this message.)") are unchanged. Docs updated (`docs/reactions-and-replies.md`).

## Tests
- `feedback_made_in_the_same_second_as_the_bots_reply_is_told_once` (integration, deterministic): pins the 👎 and the bot's reply to the same second via `exec_raw_for_test`, then checks that the next turn isn't told again and that the history mark stays. **It fails on main 1b581a9** ("told twice") and passes with the fix.
- `a_reaction_told_once_is_not_new_even_in_the_same_second_as_the_reply` (lib): told once; the same reaction again isn't news; a changed or re-set one is; telling a stale reaction leaves the changed one untold.
- `a_database_from_before_told_gets_the_column_and_keeps_its_reactions` (lib): rebuilds the #296 table without `told`, reopens the database, and checks that the column is added and an untold reaction is still news.
- Locally: `reactions_replies_test` passed 7/7 tests on 5 runs in a row on the final head, plus 2 more runs under 2 CPU burners. `--lib` passed 967/967. `clippy --lib --test reactions_replies_test -D warnings` is clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

 These migrations are additive and idempotent, and run in `Database::open`:
 
-- **`message_reactions`:** columns `message_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES messages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `reaction TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (reaction IN ('up','down'))`, `created_at` and `answered INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.
+- **`message_reactions`:** columns `message_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES messages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `reaction TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (reaction IN ('up','down'))`, `created_at`, `answered INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and `told INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.
   - There's one reaction per message, because kwant has a single person.
   - A reaction goes away with its message.
   - `answered` is 1 when the reaction started a turn. A changed reaction resets it to 0.
+  - `told` is 1 once a turn's prompt carried the reaction as feedback. A changed reaction resets it to 0. On an older database the column is added only if it's missing.
 - **`messages.reply_to_message_id TEXT NULL`:** the column is added only if it's missing.
 
 ## `PUT /api/messages/:id/reaction`
@@ -99,7 +100,7 @@ For a 👎, reconsider that message briefly: say what you'd change, or ask what
 A 👍 or 👎 never approves an approval card, a payment, a human step or a decision card: those keep their own buttons, and only the person's click on them counts.
 ```
 
-Each excerpt is plain text, up to 120 characters. The note appears once, because after the bot's reply the reactions are older than its last message.
+Each excerpt is plain text, up to 120 characters. The note appears once: putting a reaction in a turn's note marks it `told`, and later notes leave told reactions out. This holds even when the reaction and the bot's reply were made in the same second, since timestamps have 1-second precision. A reaction made before the bot's last reply isn't listed either.
 
 In history, which covers every engine and the API drivers, a reacted bot message ends with `(The person reacted 👍 to this message.)`. Only the prompt changes; the stored text stays as it is.
